articles.excerpt: A full disk can degrade system performance, cause services to fail, and even prevent you from logging in or accessing essential directories, so keeping an eye on disk usage is a core part of running a…
articles.body: A full disk can degrade system performance, cause services to fail, and even prevent you from logging in or accessing essential directories, so keeping an eye on disk usage is a core part of running any Linux machine. Linux ships with built-in command-line tools — df , du , and find — that let you see how much storage is used, how much is available, and which files or directories are eating it up. This guide walks through practical examples of each tool so you can check disk space, analyze mounted file systems, and troubleshoot disk-related issues efficiently. By the end, you'll have a working set of commands for monitoring disk usage and tracking down large files on any Linux system.

articles.title: Optimizing GPU Resource Planning with NVIDIA Dynamo
articles.excerpt: GPU resource allocation for LLM inference presents complex optimization challenges. Workloads exhibit variable request patterns, unpredictable sequence lengths, and strict latency requirements, making…
articles.body: GPU resource allocation for LLM inference presents complex optimization challenges. Workloads exhibit variable request patterns, unpredictable sequence lengths, and strict latency requirements, making static GPU allocation inefficient. Overprovisioning wastes expensive compute resources, while underprovisioning violates service level agreements (SLAs) and degrades user experience. NVIDIA Dynamo's SLA Planner automates GPU resource management through SLA-driven profiling and intelligent autoscaling, analyzing performance requirements (time-to-first-token, inter-token latency), profiling workload characteristics, and dynamically adjusting GPU worker replicas to meet latency targets while minimizing resource consumption.

Instead of relying only on plain prompts, MCP structures key information — like user identity, goals, memory, and tools — so models can act more consistently across sessions, apps, and environments. This guide walks through running a sample MCP server built with FastMCP, backed by an SQLite database, and bridging it to your local Claude Desktop application using a local mcp-proxy . By the end, you'll have a remote MCP server exposing natural-language-powered database endpoints that Claude Desktop can query directly. 1. articles.body: Building an Explainable AI-Powered Lead Scoring Engine with FastAPI Introduction Sales teams often receive many leads, but not every prospect is equally likely to become a customer. Manually reviewing every lead takes time and makes it difficult to identify the most promising opportunities. I built a personal project called the Lead Qualification and Scoring Engine to explore how AI and rule-based business logic can work together to solve this problem. The application evaluates lead information, checks Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) fit, calculates a score from 0 to 100, and generates a lead classification and recommended next action. In this article, I’ll explain the architecture, scoring approach, API design, and engineering lessons behind the project.

articles.excerpt: The Legend of Zelda is best understood as a series of fairy tales that are meant to be passed down to generations.
articles.body: In the lead-up to the Ocarina of Time ’s Switch 2 remake , I’ve spent a lot of time trying to nail down what makes the Legend of Zelda series so special. You could chalk a lot of its success up to pure design, as Nintendo has hammered out how to create a grand adventure game, whether it's working with pixels or an enormous 3D world. articles.body: Today on Decoder , I’m joined by Joey Brookhart, an analyst at the chip and AI research firm SemiAnalysis, to help me dig into the story inside the numbers of the Anthropic IPO filing — a document known as an S-1. Anthropic just filed its S-1 to go public on the Nasdaq, and it could start trading as soon as next month at a valuation of anywhere between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. That would immediately make it one of the most valuable companies on the planet. But the price tag really isn’t the whole story here. The S-1 document published earlier this week is hundreds upon hundreds of pages filled with details that finally paint a picture of the economics of a frontier AI lab.
